new_statements.quote: Ударение обычно падает на последний слог слова.
new_statements.translation: Stress usually falls on the last syllable of the word.
new_statements.citation: Дмитриева, Л. В. 1997. Барабинских татар язык. In: Э. Р. Тенишев et al. (eds.), Языки мира: Тюркские языки. Москва: Индрик, pp. 199-205.
new_statements.locator: p. 201, end of sec. 5.1.0 (Фонологические сведения), immediately before 5.1.1 (syllable structures)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (7 image-only pages, no text layer; only eng tesseract on our machine, so read from the page images). The held page image carries the running head "Л.В.Дмитриева. Барабинских татар язык 201"; the third line of the page, the last paragraph of sec. 5.1.0 (which opens on p. 200 as "5.1.0. Фонологические сведения. Фонемный состав: 12 гласных." with vowel and consonant tables), reads exactly "Ударение обычно падает на последний слог слова." and is immediately followed by "5.1.1. Допустимые структуры слога: VC, CV, CVC, реже — V, CVCC". The quote is verbatim at the stated locator. The preceding text of 5.1.0 covers vowel shifts toward Volga-Tatar vocalism, consonant distribution, sinharmon…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is normally on the final syllable of the word (i.e. on the last stem or suffix syllable, the usual Turkic pattern). The RAS 'Malye jazyki Rossii' sketch of Siberian Tatar as a whole says the same: 'Ударение обычно падает на последний слог слова или аффикс, что характерно для тюркских языков' (stress usually falls on the last syllable of the word or on the affix, as is characteristic of Turkic languages), adding that unstressed vowels undergo only quantitative, not qualitative, reduction.
new_statements.exceptions: None specified; 'обычно' (usually) implies unstated exceptions (presumably the usual Turkic non-final cases), but neither source lists them.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (последний слог слова); citation forms implied. Dmitrieva's chapter describes the Baraba dialect (Novosibirsk oblast, ~8,000 speakers per the chapter), transcribed after Radlov; the minlang sketch covers Siberian Tatar generally with Tobol-Irtysh (Tyumen) material.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is from Dmitrieva's chapter on the Baraba dialect (барабинский диалект, Novosibirsk oblast), which Glottolog 5.1 subsumes under Siberian Tatar sibe1250 [sty] without a separate dialect glottocode. The corroborating whole-language statement (final syllable or affix) is from the Institute of Linguistics RAS 'Малые языки России' sketch, whose material is Tobol-Irtysh (Tyumen); no first-hand statement for the Tomsk dialect was found.
